One thing that always bothered me about reddit (and some other websites) is that when comments that had replies attached to them were deleted, it was almost always impossible to follow any conversation afterward. I understand Whoaverse is very serious about privacy and protecting information, however, so I propose a 'meet-in-the-middle' sort of solution. 1) You can 'detach' your name from a comment (or your user will be automatically detached if you delete your account), but the comment will remain visible IF there are replies/posts linked to it. Any karma, however, will continue to affect you. This would deter people from simply unlinking their name to a very unpopular comment in order to salvage karma points. However, in the spirit of keeping this site less "mean girls" and more supportive, this could potentially prevent a certain user from getting constantly hounded and downvoted just because of one comment. Additionally, admins would still have full visibility, so they could track a "negative" or "spam" user and take necessary action, but again, that would be up to the admins or moderators as opposed to butthurt users with way too much time on their hands. 2) Comments can be deleted completely only if no one has interacted with it (votes or reply)

The other thing- and I sincerely apologize if this has been discussed elsewhere, but I've been trying my best to read around and have yet to find a comment addressing this specifically- I'm not such a big fan of the upvote/downvote threshold. I fully support the reason for its implementation, but I think it is too large and does more harm than good. For a casual user, getting 100 comment karma could take a very long time (I'm talking months). Even IF you participate in discussions and post a healthy three to five times per day (and assuming those posts get upvoted), it would take weeks. Especially for a site this new that needs active users that want to come back and participate, this could potentially be detrimental. Casual users are just as important as the power users who spend more than an hour a day on the site. If Whoaverse wants to grow, it needs to keep them in mind as well. It is too discouraging to have to achieve so much in order to simply participate.

Again, I do understand why the rule was put in place, however, so maybe a compromise? As of now, I understand even lurkers get 10 upvotes. Build upon that. How about, have users start off with 10 upvotes and 1 downvote. Then, as they post and become more active, that threshold grows as well- so say, after 5 positive comment points, they get upgraded to 15 upvotes and 3 downvotes. 10 positive would be 25 uv/5 dv. That 100 karma should be the threshold for unlimited upvotes and downvotes, but not the minimum to even start downvoting or have more than 10 uploads a day.

I know that this would be complicated to implement, and I know that it may sound like crazy to some of you super users that probably have no problem achieving that, but for the casual user that is a huge difference. It's simply discouraging to not be considered a valuable member of the community right away- such limits send the message that only the opinions of those who spend more than 2 or 3 hours (or more!) a day on the site matter. I do agree with its purpose of keeping the "haters" at bay, but it also limits contribution from new members who want to feel as if their opinion matters and want to have an immediate impact on the community. It's good to encourage users to participate, but more often times than not, casual users (like myself) don't like commenting for the sake of commenting. If I have something new or insightful to add, I post it. If not, I use my upvote/downvote power to agree (or disagree) with what people have already said. So having that ability limited really does make me feel as if my ability to contribute is limited. Of course, there are people out there that ruin it for everyone, so I do agree with a policy that deters that, but it would be nice to at least have a "level" system like the one suggested. That way, users can work up to "unlimited" status at reasonable intervals, spammers/rabid downvoters still are hindered, and everyone wins =D

Thus, if delinking were to be implemented, there would also need to be a way to decide whether a comment can be tracked back to the author through content clues. If it were a moderator's job, it would add an unnecessary complication because they will have to decide whether to allow delinking or editing the comment to remove information that suggests who the author is.

Isn't it in everyone's understanding that if they post something willingly online, it will stay there?

You actually partially changed my mind on the subject here. However, how it will be moderated needs to be discussed.

Honestly, it seems like it only truly benefits those karma whores and people that obsess over their score (for whatever reason, maybe they validate themselves based on that, who knows) because then they can just delete unpopular comments and voila. Like a cop out.

The problem with this statement is that we need not worry about the karma status of other users to which you are referencing in the latter part of your sentence.

There are a number of reasons why users should always have to ability to delete their comments. One reason is because, perhaps, they may have changed their mind about the comment and they want to remove it from the discussion to prevent additional downvoting when they do not stand by the comment anymore.

I understand your stance on the matter and in regards to this topic, so I suggest a compromise: when a comment is 'delinked', karma at that point, positive or negative, should count towards the user. However, the current vote count should be frozen and additional voting should be disabled to protect against voting brigades or the situation I have mentioned above.

The only problem I see with this compromise is that the delinked comments would start to sink to the bottom as other comments receive points. However, I believe that it is better than orphaning thoughtful discussions.
